detail: Within 5% of the high counts as close to the top, and the S&P 500 closed at 7,561.67 on Friday, about 3.3% below its record close of 7,818.93 on 6 October. It still rose 2.5% over the week, its best week since August.
source: AP closing figures, 13 Nov; record close from Anadolu and EdgeX, 6 Oct

detail: Breadth was mixed on Friday: more than 60% of S&P 500 companies rose even as the index fell, but across all Nasdaq-listed shares 214 hit new 52-week lows against 28 new highs. Big companies held up while many smaller ones kept sliding, so the picture under the surface is split.
source: thetrading.tools (Nasdaq-listed new highs and lows), 13 Nov; AP and Morningstar via Decode News (S&P 500 risers), 13 Nov

detail: Above 4.5% counts as high, and the US 10-year yield closed at 5.15% on Friday, up from 5.10% on Thursday, as US producer prices kept inflation worries alive. Safe government bonds paying over 5% set a high bar for shares to beat.
source: Yahoo Finance via Globicus and BuyOrBeSold, 13 Nov

detail: Markets expect rates to go up: CME FedWatch shows a quarter-point Fed rise on 9 December as close to certain, with a small chance of a half-point move, and economists at ING expect another Bank of England rise by February. Higher rates make borrowing dearer and tend to weigh on share prices, especially fast-growing companies.
source: CME FedWatch via BeInCrypto and Pepperstone, 15 to 16 Nov; ING via MT Newswires, 12 Nov

detail: Above $90 a barrel counts as expensive, and Brent crude settled at $95.84 on Friday, barely changed on the day as Middle East headlines pulled it both ways. Dear oil keeps pressure on inflation, which is one reason central banks are raising rates.
source: Settlement price via Decode News (AP, Morningstar), 13 Nov
